correctness.rationale: A core vertex outside the closed neighborhood of the projected seeds is not observed in the first step and cannot be the first target of a force: each neighboring core lacks an initially observed private leaf and cannot force that leaf while the target remains unobserved. A private leaf cannot deliver a first observation of its own unobserved core. Thus the projection dominates and selecting an optimum all-core domination set attains the bound. At minimum each selected index receives one core/leaf mark. In each length-three gap the internal vertex on a leaf-marked side cannot be observed from the other internal vertex before its own observation, by the same private-leaf obstruction. Therefore a leaf mark between two long gaps blocks, and a length-two gap with two leaf marks blocks if neither end can start propagation from its other side. In an adjacent two-short-gap cluster with three endpoints, an all-leaf assignment is blocked; any core mark starts forcing across the cluster, because it observes an intermediate and a leaf-marked endpoint with one observed core neighbor can force its other one. A length-one gap supplies each of its selected endpoints an already observed neighbor even with two leaf marks. The n=4 case has the same two endpoints on both short gaps and must be counted separately. The resulting admissible counts per pattern are 1 (all long), 3 (one length-two), 4 (one length-one), 7 or 9 (two length-two gaps adjacent or disjoint, k≥3) and 3 for the opposite pair at n=4. Cyclic marking counts adjacent double-short gaps in n ways and disjoint ones in n(k-3)/2, giving the displayed formula. A separate adjacency-set enumeration of all subsets through the claimed minimum for n=3–8 found no smaller successes and recovered 3,22,15,3,77,24. This is corroboration; the gap argument proves all orders. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.
